scope: Python cross-module same-name call binding found by the M2.5-D experiment
root_cause: codegraph-server's resolve_cross_file_imports built one global name -> NodeId map. Duplicate free functions were collapsed to the highest-weight/first declaration, and import-symbol edges also used that global map. `from pricing import apply_discount` therefore resolved to legacy.apply_discount.

behavior: index CodeFile paths, path suffixes, Python files, and module-level symbols per file
build per-file import bindings for `from module import name` and `import module [as alias]`
Python call resolution order: qualified/inherited -> imported symbol -> module alias -> ambiguous method -> duplicate free function unresolved -> global fallback
Python import edges use the same binding; ambiguous symbols get no edge
non-Python resolution keeps the previous global fallback
not_fixed: per-symbol aliases (`from m import x as y`) were not extracted at this commit; a call could stay unresolved or bind a unique global homonym named `y` (fixed by PYTHON-ALIAS-BINDING-2026-11-25)
`relation:` refs in archmeld.map.txt remain unimplemented; the binding prerequisite is now met, but the syntax/resolution is a separate E3/E5 task

server_lib.note: the 17 failures are in backend workspace-path helpers, handlers, the ai_query performance threshold and the memory path format; none are watcher or cross-file resolution tests, and the watcher module is 29/29

limitations: the fix changes the cross-file resolver, not the Python parser; per-symbol aliases remain for the follow-up PYTHON-ALIAS-BINDING slice
the full codegraph-server lib suite has 17 unrelated/environmental failures (402 passed / 1 ignored); the watcher module is 29/29 and the export fixtures pass
archmeld relation refs are still unimplemented even though the Python binding prerequisite is now met
